Contracts.purpose: Describe and negotiate public contracts before using their operations. A contract declaration identifies schemas and versions; it does not grant permission to perform the declared effects.
Contracts.sequence: Define contracts during the allowed registration stage, then query compatibility and availability. A successful schema check validates the value against that schema; domain ownership and effect checks still apply.
Contracts.limits: WatchAvailability returns a subscription. Refresh dependent UI after availability changes, but do not silently rebind a required service to a different provider.

Definitions.purpose: Publish typed definitions into registries and resolve the definitions visible to a consumer. Definitions are data; registering one does not make arbitrary launcher code execute it.
Definitions.sequence: Discover the registry and its accepted schema first. Register owned values during staging, and use the returned identity and revision for later updates. Tags and overlays affect resolution according to the registry contract.
Definitions.limits: Use ExplainResolution when an overlay or tag produces an unexpected result. Keep a failed resolution distinct from a valid empty result; remove only definitions owned by the current load.

Predicates.purpose: Declare and evaluate bounded conditions for workflows and other authorized consumers. A predicate computes a result; it must not smuggle a mutation into a query callback.
Predicates.sequence: Register the input schema and handler or supported expression, then evaluate with matching inputs. The runtime supports a closed expression grammar rather than arbitrary source evaluation.
Predicates.limits: Treat an evaluation failure separately from false. A missing capability, bad schema or retired handler is not evidence that the business condition is false.

Actions.purpose: Expose a named, typed operation that the Host can invoke with the declared effects and confirmation policy. An action connects a descriptor to a callback; a registered callback alone is not a public action.
Actions.sequence: Register the descriptor during initialization. Call Invoke after activation with matching inputs and the required idempotency key. Inspect the returned operation through Tasks.
Actions.limits: Confirmation occurs before handler dispatch. Decline must not invoke the handler. Reusing a mutation key with changed inputs is a conflict; an unknown result must not be replayed with a new key.

Commands.purpose: Discover and execute Host-exposed commands through typed action contracts. A command ID names a public operation, not an arbitrary shell command or executable.
Commands.sequence: List or describe the command, validate its input schema, then Execute with the same target and inputs the user reviewed. Execution returns an operation to observe.
Commands.limits: An unavailable command remains unavailable even if a similarly named UI control exists. Do not fall back to process execution or private UI access.

Workflows.purpose: Compose registered actions and predicates into bounded, observable work. Workflow definitions describe ordering, branches, retries and recovery; they do not bypass each node’s permissions.
Workflows.sequence: Register and validate the definition before activation. Start with typed inputs, then read or watch the operation. Persistent recovery requires the saved revision, unchanged definition and compatible inputs.
Workflows.limits: Resume known progress only. OUTCOME_UNKNOWN records an effect whose result cannot be established; it is not a failed step that is automatically safe to retry.

Schedules.purpose: Trigger an owned workflow at a declared time, interval or event. Scheduling determines when work is requested; the workflow still performs normal authority checks.
Schedules.sequence: Register the schedule with a valid timezone and trigger definition. Enable or disable it explicitly, inspect ReadNextRun, and use TriggerNow for an intentional manual run.
Schedules.limits: Missed-trigger policies govern backlog, not exactly-once effects. Disabling or stopping fences future dispatch; it does not undo effects already completed by a run.

Events.purpose: Publish typed events and subscribe with explicit delivery and resumption behavior. Event payloads describe observations; the Host supplies trusted origin and invocation identity.
Events.sequence: Define the event contract, subscribe during the permitted registration stage, and publish only with the declared schema and scope. Keep the returned subscription identity for cleanup.
Events.limits: Callbacks may repeat under at-least-once delivery. Handle resynchronization after gaps and retention loss. Use the matching subscription-based unsubscribe operation instead of reinterpreting a subscription as a registration.

State.purpose: Expose a current, revisioned value and observe changes. State is useful for a view of current data; event history and private durable storage serve different purposes.
State.sequence: Define the owned state and schema, then read a snapshot before a conditional update. Pass the exact returned revision to CompareExchangeOwned and reconcile conflicts.
State.limits: A watch can report a gap; recover with a fresh Read. Uninitialized state is explicit and must not be confused with a failed read or with a valid empty value.

UI.purpose: Contribute verified NXML pages, components and finite UI behavior to Host-owned rendering. Plugins provide assets and typed intent; the Host owns controls, input, navigation and confirmation.
UI.sequence: Open verified package assets before registration. Discover extension targets and their contracts before contributing or replacing a view. Keep action IDs and NXML bindings in the plugin namespace.
UI.limits: Stage registrations are not visible before atomic activation. Stop retires them. Model updates, drawing surfaces and input subscriptions retain their own schemas, budgets and ownership checks.

Plugins.purpose: Export a typed service or bind to a compatible service from another admitted plugin. Bindings are explicit relationships between particular loads, not ambient access to other plugins.
Plugins.sequence: Export during Initialize, bind during PostInitialize and probe during Checkup. Invoke only after activation. Describe the service before choosing a version range.
Plugins.limits: A required provider dependency can stop its consumers when it retires; an optional binding becomes unavailable. Bindings never silently switch to a replacement load.

Diagnostics.purpose: Report bounded, structured information about the current plugin’s work. Diagnostics help explain a failure without exposing private account data or creating an unbounded logging channel.
Diagnostics.sequence: Use stable message keys and relevant operation/correlation IDs. ReadOwnReports is scoped to the caller; it is not a global launcher log reader.
Diagnostics.limits: The Host assigns source and ownership. Do not log bearer tokens, grants, encrypted package keys or full user file contents. A diagnostic report does not turn a failed operation into success.

Resources.purpose: Register cleanup and release owned registrations or subscriptions. This group coordinates specific resource kinds; it is not a universal release API for every opaque value.
Resources.sequence: Retain each acquisition’s actual handle type. ReadSubscription consumes a bounded batch, so retain the same key while resolving an uncertain read. Release a subscription when it is no longer needed.
Resources.limits: A gap requires a new authoritative snapshot or domain-specific resynchronization. Stopped loads cannot reuse prior handles; do not cast blobs or files to RegistrationRef.

Minecraft.Instances.purpose: Read the launcher’s instance inventory and request supported instance changes. An instance identity is a Host-owned reference, not a directory name or a plugin-selected filesystem path.
Minecraft.Instances.sequence: List within the requested inventory scope, read details by returned identity, and prepare changes before committing the exact plan. Selection and launch are separate operations.
Minecraft.Instances.limits: Several clone/delete routes remain unmapped in the recorded Host. Do not emulate them by deleting files through unrelated APIs. Read errors must remain distinct from an empty inventory.

Minecraft.Install.purpose: Resolve an installation draft into an explicit plan and execute it through the launcher’s installer. Draft edits, plan validation and execution are separate steps.
Minecraft.Install.sequence: List compatible game/loader versions, update and validate the draft, resolve its plan, review it, then execute that plan. Monitor the returned operation for actual completion.
Minecraft.Install.limits: An accepted execution request does not prove all files installed. Recovery and custom loader/template registration remain unavailable where marked; do not fabricate recovery records.

Minecraft.Java.purpose: Discover Java runtimes, inspect requirements and select a runtime through launcher policy. Managed distribution offers describe the complete installable content accepted by the current installer.
Minecraft.Java.sequence: Read the instance’s requirements before resolving selection. Use ListManagedDistributions and PrepareManagedInstall for the mapped multi-file distribution path, then commit through Install.
Minecraft.Java.limits: The older single-file distribution catalog and preparation route are not mapped in this snapshot. A selected runtime still needs platform, architecture and version compatibility.

Minecraft.Launch.purpose: Prepare and start a game using an explicit profile and launch plan. Profile editing, plan creation and process observation are different lifecycle steps.
Minecraft.Launch.sequence: Read or select the intended instance profile, prepare the launch, validate the exact plan, then Start. Observe the attempt and resulting session rather than assuming admission means a running game.
Minecraft.Launch.limits: A changed account, Java selection or instance state can invalidate the plan. Contribution/preflight registration routes remain unmapped where listed; arbitrary native command injection is not a fallback.

Minecraft.Processes.purpose: Observe game sessions owned by the launcher and request session lifecycle actions. A session ID is not a raw operating-system PID.
Minecraft.Processes.sequence: List sessions, read a selected session, and subscribe to bounded log or metric updates. Use RequestClose for the supported graceful path; Stop has separate termination semantics.
Minecraft.Processes.limits: Missing metrics are not measured zero. A log subscription can lose history; use the supported range read and gap handling. Closing a launcher view must not imply killing a game session.

Minecraft.Content.purpose: Inspect and change instance content with dependency-aware plans and transaction records. A content item belongs to a specific instance and content domain.
Minecraft.Content.sequence: Build the relevant install/enable/disable/remove/update plan, inspect the preview and execute its exact identity/revision. Read the operation and transaction records before offering rollback.
Minecraft.Content.limits: Rollback is a reviewed domain operation, not arbitrary file reversal. Import/export supports an explicit format allowlist. Trash clearing and custom format providers remain unavailable where marked.

Minecraft.Worlds.purpose: Read world metadata and request supported copy, rename, data-pack and backup operations. A world belongs to an instance; its display name does not grant path access.
Minecraft.Worlds.sequence: Read the world identity and health, then prepare data-pack changes or other planned operations. Use the returned task to observe long-running copies and backups.
Minecraft.Worlds.limits: Delete and restore routes are not fully mapped in this snapshot. Never substitute a live directory overwrite for an unavailable restore operation.

Minecraft.Servers.purpose: Manage the saved server list, query status, discover LAN announcements and request joining through the launcher. Discovery and status are observations, not launch authorization.
Minecraft.Servers.sequence: Preserve the saved list’s revision when updating it. Read status through the Host resolver; consume LAN discovery as a subscription and handle disappearance or gaps.
Minecraft.Servers.limits: An unreachable status probe is not definitive proof a server never accepts clients. Joining still requires a compatible instance and account; do not convert a server address into arbitrary process arguments.

Catalog.purpose: Search resource providers and resolve projects, versions, files and dependencies. Provider identity remains part of every resource reference and page sequence.
Catalog.sequence: Choose an explicit provider, search with a bounded page, then resolve a selected version before planning installation. Read-provider callbacks return typed values with matching provenance.
Catalog.limits: Custom catalog providers currently support seven read queries. Mixed built-in/custom searches, custom installation and favorites are not implied by successful registration.

Accounts.purpose: Read public account information and request account workflows without exposing credentials. Authentication tokens and launch credentials are not ordinary account metadata.
Accounts.sequence: Begin sign-in, present its challenge through the supported user flow, then continue or cancel with the returned identity. Check launch eligibility before requesting a scoped launch grant.
Accounts.limits: Public reads do not authorize token extraction. Sign-out and custom account providers remain unmapped where listed. A cancelled challenge is not a successful sign-in.

Settings.purpose: Read effective settings and apply reviewed changes to the requested scope. Stored values, inherited values and temporary overlays have different ownership and lifetimes.
Settings.sequence: Use GetEffective when the UI needs the value and its origin. Preview a change and apply its plan; retain an overlay’s registration so it can be ended explicitly.
Settings.limits: A temporary overlay is not a durable profile write. Schema/page registration and migration routes remain unmapped where listed; direct modification of launcher configuration files is not a supported substitute.

Themes.purpose: Inspect themes, preview a prepared theme and commit or revert it through Host appearance ownership. Preview is a temporary visible effect, not merely a query.
Themes.sequence: Prepare the selected theme, preview the returned plan if desired, then commit it or revert the preview registration. Edit theme options using the current revision.
Themes.limits: A failed candidate should not erase the last valid appearance. Resource and migration routes remain unmapped where listed; Theme.ReleaseResource must not be used as a generic blob-release mechanism.

Backups.purpose: Inspect and maintain the selected instance’s durable backup history. The recorded Host maps 11 of 14 operations through the Setup owner, using a separate content-addressed store for each instance. Global backup history is not exposed.
Backups.sequence: Obtain an instance ID from Minecraft.Instances.List, then call Backups.List. Keep the returned page revision for prune and retention updates. Capture and prune require a single-use plan and Host confirmation. Observe the returned operation through Tasks until it reaches a terminal state, then refresh the history.
Backups.limits: Capture currently accepts only a null Target and empty Include/Exclude arrays. Retention supports 1–1,024 copies and 1–3,650 days, with MaximumBytes=0; it governs explicit prune previews, not automatic scheduling. Export writes a thin JSON manifest without file contents. PreviewRestore, Restore and Import remain unavailable: their original request models do not express the required new-directory or instance target safely.

Downloads.purpose: Resolve and run downloads as observable Host tasks with verification and cancellation. A download plan identifies approved sources and expected content.
Downloads.sequence: Resolve the plan, start it, then read or watch progress. Verify the final content before using it. Pause and resume availability depends on the admitted operation and transfer behavior.
Downloads.limits: A completed transport is not proof of a matching hash. Custom source-resolver and transfer-provider routes remain unmapped; do not infer them from built-in download support.

Tasks.purpose: Create and observe bounded records of work. A task communicates progress and terminal results; it is not permission to perform the underlying business action.
Tasks.sequence: For plugin-owned work, CreateOwned, Report progress, then Complete or Fail exactly as the result warrants. For Host work, read/watch the returned operation and request cancellation through its supported route.
Tasks.limits: Dismiss terminal records when no longer needed. Retry is not mapped in the current Desktop snapshot; a generic retry button must not replay unknown effects with fresh keys.

Storage.purpose: Persist private plugin data in authorized namespaces with revision checks and transactions. Namespace handles are scoped to the admitted load even when the persisted data survives restart.
Storage.sequence: Open the namespace, read before conditional writes, and use CompareExchange for competing updates. Commit a transaction only with its actual returned identity and revision.
Storage.limits: Migration is explicit and bounded. A failed or oversized migration must not reset the store. The storage implementation assumes one trusted Host owner; it is not a distributed database protocol.

Files.purpose: Access verified package assets and Host-granted user files. Paths and opaque FileRef values have different meanings; a displayed path is not an access grant.
Files.sequence: Open a package asset by its declared relative path or request a user picker grant. Read bounded data, use atomic replacement for writes, and prepare move/delete plans before execution.
Files.limits: Do not expand a grant to siblings or symlink targets outside its scope. Payload integrity and filesystem authority are checked separately. Cancellation from a picker is not a selected empty file.

Network.purpose: Perform authorized network operations with explicit request/connection identities, bounded payloads and cancellation. This capability is not unrestricted socket access.
Network.sequence: Use the Host’s approved request or connection route, read bounded responses, and close owned connections when finished. Receiving consumes external state and is restricted to Active.
Network.limits: Timeout can leave an external mutation outcome unknown. A redirect or resolved address remains subject to Host policy; do not retry through another transport to bypass a denied destination.

Platform.purpose: Request finite operating-system integration through the Host. Platform availability, user grants and application policy determine which actions can run.
Platform.sequence: Describe the platform or query its facts before presenting optional features. Use explicit URI, file and clipboard operations with the requested data type and scope.
Platform.limits: Opening a URI is an external effect, not arbitrary command execution. Unsupported display/power/clipboard data must remain unavailable rather than being reported as fabricated measurements.

Minecraft.Diagnostics.purpose: Analyze an instance and preview a repair using the launcher’s diagnostic owner. Findings identify suspected conditions; a finding alone does not authorize a write.
Minecraft.Diagnostics.sequence: Analyze the selected instance, review the returned findings, then prepare and confirm a supported repair plan. Execute the exact plan and observe its task.
Minecraft.Diagnostics.limits: Custom rule providers remain unmapped. Preserve unresolved findings and failed repairs; do not report an instance healthy simply because a provider could not run.

operations.Events.Unsubscribe: This historical current-catalog method accepts RegistrationRequest, not SubscriptionRef. Use UnsubscribeSubscription for a handle returned by Subscribe, or RegisterSubscription when both identities are needed. Never reinterpret one handle as the other.
operations.Events.UnsubscribeSubscription: Accepts the actual SubscriptionRef returned by Subscribe. This additive operation resolves the historical mismatch between Subscribe and Unsubscribe.
operations.Events.RegisterSubscription: Returns EventSubscriptionRegistration, carrying the subscription and registration identities explicitly. Retain the correct member for each cleanup API.
operations.Minecraft.Java.PrepareManagedInstall: Use an offer returned by ListManagedDistributions. The managed offer describes the installer’s multi-file manifest; it is not interchangeable with the older JavaDistribution model.
operations.Tasks.Retry: Retry an owned failed/cancelled task where the owner defines replay semantics. Plugin-created tasks reset to Pending under the same ID and a new revision; the plugin must perform and report the work again. Failed workflows use the workflow journal and its recovery rules. Running/completed tasks, foreign tasks and unknown outcomes are rejected. Arbitrary Host file/network/game operations are not implicitly replayed; prepare a new domain plan instead.
operations.Resources.ReadSubscription: The current runtime consumes up to 256 queued items. Repeat an uncertain read with the same idempotency key to retrieve the corresponding batch; a new key is a new consumption request.
operations.UI.RegisterPage: The page asset must be opened from the verified package and owned by the current load. The descriptor links an NXML asset to its model schema and declared actions; it does not transfer rendering ownership.
operations.Files.OpenPackageFile: Path is a normalized relative payload path, such as page.nxml. It must identify an admitted package asset. The returned FileRef can be passed to UI registration; it does not grant access to the surrounding installation directory.
operations.Accounts.ReadPublic: Only public metadata is returned. Account tokens and credentials are not made available by this method or by a successful read permission check.
operations.Catalog.RegisterProvider: The current mapped custom provider family is read-only. It supports Search, ReadProject, ListVersions, ReadVersion, ReadChangelog, ResolveFiles and ResolveDependencies. See the provider guide for descriptor and callback requirements.
operations.Themes.Preview: Returns a registration for the temporary preview. Retain it for Revert; the preview itself does not mean the theme is durably selected.
operations.Storage.Migrate: The current migration boundary accepts at most 256 entries and invokes an owned read-only migration action. Read the resulting operation to obtain the new namespace; do not reuse an obsolete namespace revision.
operations.Actions.Invoke: The Host can request user confirmation before dispatch. A declined or cancelled prompt must not run the handler. The OperationRef is for observing the action result, not proof of callback success.
operations.Workflows.Resume: Recovery requires the saved run revision and unchanged workflow definition/input. An unknown effect cannot be converted to a known failed step and automatically replayed.
operations.State.CompareExchangeOwned: Use the revision from the latest authoritative snapshot. On conflict, re-read and reconcile; do not increment or synthesize a revision token.
operations.Storage.Write: The recorded storage owner requires the existing entry’s exact revision for an update. An absent ExpectedRevision creates only a missing key; it does not mean unconditional overwrite.
operations.Storage.CompareExchange: Read the entry first and supply its exact revision. For a missing key, use an absent revision. A competing create/update fails with STALE_REVISION; both Write and CompareExchange enforce this rule in the recorded owner.
operations.Backups.List: Id is an admitted instance ID. The page contains that instance’s complete bounded history (at most 1,024 snapshots), no continuation cursor, and a scope revision covering manifests and retention. Use this page revision for BackupPrune.ExpectedRevision and BackupRetention.ExpectedRevision. Backup IDs belong to this plugin load; refresh them after reload.
operations.Backups.Read: Id is a backup ID returned by List, not an instance ID. A pruned backup returns NOT_FOUND; a fabricated or foreign-load ID returns HANDLE_INVALID. Size is the logical sum of referenced file sizes, not physical CAS storage.
operations.Backups.Statistics: Id is an instance ID. Count is its snapshot count; Bytes sums logical sizes across snapshots and therefore counts shared content more than once. This does not report the launcher-wide store or reclaimed disk space.
operations.Backups.PrepareCapture: Instance must be current. Set Target=null and Include/Exclude to empty arrays; other valid selections return CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. The plan binds the instance and library revision, expires after ten minutes and requires Host confirmation. Only the instance directory is captured; shared assets, shared libraries, Java and account data are outside this snapshot. Capture bounds are 8,192 files, 512 MiB per file and 8 GiB in total; sources overlapping the backup store or containing unsupported links are rejected by the owner.
operations.Backups.Capture: Consume the plan from PrepareCapture once, with its exact revision. Host confirmation and instance revision are checked before execution. The owner rejects non-idle capture and changing source files. A completed task has result schema Empty; refresh List to obtain backup IDs. An OperationRef only acknowledges admission, not successful capture.
operations.Backups.VerifyOffline: Id is a listed backup ID. The owner verifies the referenced immutable objects and their hashes. Valid=false means missing or corrupt bytes; Issues lists up to 256 affected relative paths. A thin manifest alone can be listed but is not evidence of offline readiness. This checks snapshot bytes, not whether the game can launch offline with its Java, shared assets and libraries.
operations.Backups.Export: Backup must be a listed backup ID and File a load-owned writable file grant. The Host confirms the destination, writes a staged thin JSON manifest and commits without overwriting an existing file. The completed task returns FileRef. No file contents are embedded: label this as a thin manifest, not a portable full backup, and explain that another store still needs every referenced object.
operations.Backups.PreviewPrune: Use the scope revision from List. Retention.MaximumBytes must be zero; unsupported byte limits return CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. The plan summarizes the number of manifests to remove and bytes to reclaim. The newest snapshot is always retained. Changing the history after preview invalidates the plan.
operations.Backups.Prune: Consume the plan from PreviewPrune once. Confirmation, scope revision, idle state and the owner’s fresh prune revision must all still pass. Deletion affects only this instance’s store. The completed task returns Empty; refresh List and Statistics. A rejected or stale plan never authorizes deletion of a different scope.
operations.Backups.ReadRetention: Id is an instance ID. Returns the stored count/day policy with MaximumBytes=0. Defaults are 32 copies and 90 days. Read List as well to obtain the revision required by SetRetention. Reading this policy does not indicate that automatic scoped cleanup is enabled.
operations.Backups.SetRetention: Use the exact revision returned by List, not a BackupSummary revision. The Host confirms the change and the owner compares the scope revision while holding its storage lease. Concurrent policy or history changes fail with CONFLICT rather than overwriting another update. Returns the committed policy; query List again before the next change.
operations.Backups.PreviewRestore: Bind an existing backup, its ExpectedRevision and a new destination admitted by PrepareRestoreDestination into a single-use restore plan. The Host preserves the source instance and never merges into an existing destination.
operations.Backups.Restore: Confirm and execute a restore plan through the owning instance backup store. The destination grant is re-resolved under the file mutation gate; missing/corrupt objects, changed revisions or an existing destination fail. Empty is returned only after restore completes.
operations.Backups.Import: Import a thin manifest into the instance scope identified by the non-null Backup anchor. Backup must be a backup already listed by this caller. For an empty scope, use ImportInto. The manifest carries metadata and hashes, not content objects; successful import is not proof of offline readiness. VerifyOffline checks that separately.
operations.Minecraft.Instances.PrepareClone: Prepare a new isolated instance in a registered destination root. Source and destination handles belong to the caller; ExpectedRevision is the source library revision. Existing destinations, reserved names, links and running games are rejected. The owner copies version files, local game data and cross-root runtime dependencies without overwriting shared files. The copy budget is 100,000 entries, depth 64, 2 GiB per file and 8 GiB total. The manifest is renamed and published last. A failed cross-root clone can leave verified shared cache files; it does not replace the source.
operations.Minecraft.Instances.CommitClone: Consume a clone plan once. The Host asks for confirmation, rechecks the source revision and destination, acquires recovery leases in canonical root order, copies and publishes the new instance, then refreshes discovery. A completed operation returns Empty. A successful admission is not proof that the clone finished.
operations.Minecraft.Instances.PrepareDelete: Prepare deletion of an admitted instance at ExpectedRevision. RetainUserData=true moves its version directory into the root’s .recycle directory. False permanently removes that directory after moving it out of the active library. Shared root data and runtime caches remain. The review text distinguishes these outcomes. Running sessions block deletion.
operations.Minecraft.Instances.CommitDelete: Consume a deletion plan after Host confirmation and an owner-side revision check. Deleting the version directory never follows child symbolic links into another directory. Empty is returned only after the owner finishes; stale or consumed plans require a new preview.
operations.Minecraft.Install.ListRecoveries: List authenticated pending new-install, modification and modpack journals under registered game roots. Completed, rolled-back and dismissed journals are omitted. Handles bind the caller, root, journal and revision. RecoveryRecord.Operation is an opaque native-task correlation ID, not a Tasks.Read handle. At most 64 roots, 4,096 journal directories and 256 pending records are admitted.
operations.Minecraft.Install.ResumeRecovery: Confirm and resume the exact listed journal using the owner’s existing authenticated recovery pipeline. Rollback-requested journals continue rollback. Re-list after a revision conflict. The returned Tasks operation tracks this resume attempt and returns Empty on completion; it is distinct from RecoveryRecord.Operation.
operations.Minecraft.Install.DiscardRecovery: Confirm dismissal of the listed journal. Existing and staged files are retained; dismissal removes the pending recovery offer. The owner rejects unfinished rollback and stale records. This operation does not delete an installed instance.
operations.Minecraft.Install.RegisterTemplate: Stage an owned template during Initialize. Workflow must name a workflow owned by the same load with InstallTemplateInvocation input and Empty output. The template declares a game version, supported built-in loaders and desired content. Instances.PrepareCreate consumes its ID; the workflow performs the installation through authorized Host APIs. Registration alone installs nothing. See the installation guide for workflow responsibilities.
operations.Minecraft.Install.RegisterLoaderProvider: Register kind nexa:install/loader-catalog with method ListVersions: LoaderVersionRequest → `Page<LoaderVersion>`. Consumers pass the provider ID as Loader in ListLoaderVersions. Returned items must use a supported built-in loader family and the requested game version. The Host wraps pagination and feeds the selections to its existing installer; this does not authorize an arbitrary executable installer.
operations.Minecraft.Java.RegisterDistributionProvi: Register kind nexa:java/distributions with method ListDistributions: PageRequest → `Page<JavaDistribution>`. The current Host accepts verified ZIP distributions. Each entry identifies this provider and supplies OS, architecture, version, exact archive size and SHA-256. Multi-file Mojang offers continue to use ListManagedDistributions and PrepareManagedInstall.
operations.Minecraft.Java.ListDistributions: Aggregate published distribution providers and filter for the current OS and architecture. There may be at most eight providers and 128 entries per provider; provider replies must have no continuation cursor. The caller’s page is applied to the combined revisioned result. An empty result means no matching registered offer.
operations.Minecraft.Java.PrepareInstall: Prepare a ZIP installation in a registered root’s `runtime/plugin-<sha256>` directory. Require Java major 8–99, matching host OS/architecture, an archive of 1–512 MiB, 1–8 HTTPS sources and a SHA-256 digest. Download.Target is replaced with a temporary Host-owned file grant. The review includes source, digest and the fact that Java will execute for probing. The owner rejects unsafe entries, caps extraction at 8,192 entries and 2 GiB total, probes exactly one bin/java executable, checks version/architecture and registers it with registry CAS. An unsuccessful registry CAS can leave a verified directory for explicit registration.
operations.Minecraft.Launch.RegisterContribution: Stage a query-only callback during Initialize. Its input and output are LaunchProfile. Declare a nonempty subset of MemoryMiB, Width and Height; every other field must remain unchanged. Definitions are ordered by qualified ID, and the first accepted contribution owns each field. Required failures abort preparation; optional failures appear in ExplainContribution. Values affect this launch only and are validated by the owner’s settings schema.
operations.Minecraft.Launch.RegisterPreflight: Stage a pure LaunchProfile → ValidationReport callback with an empty Fields array. The Host runs preflights after contributions during Prepare and again before execution. Required invalid/fatal reports block launch; optional failures are suppressed and reported. Definition retirement or revision changes invalidate prepared plans. Mutation reentrancy is denied.
operations.Minecraft.Launch.ExplainContribution: Read accepted extension IDs and suppressed issues for an owned launch plan/attempt ID. This report explains preparation; it does not assert that the game started. Use ReadAttempt for execution state.
operations.Minecraft.Content.PreviewClearTrash: Prepare a plan bound to the admitted instance and exact recognized trash IDs. The owner rejects a changed set, a running game, linked entries, more than 1,000 trash directories, more than 32,768 tree entries or depth above 64 before deleting any selected record.
operations.Minecraft.Content.ClearTrash: Consume the plan returned by PreviewClearTrash after Host confirmation. This permanently removes the recognized trash entries included in the plan. It does not accept an instance ID in place of a plan, and it cannot clear newly added trash without another preview.
operations.Minecraft.Content.RegisterFormatProvider: Register kind nexa:content/format with Inspect: ContentInspectionInput → ContentInspection. InspectWithProvider reads an explicitly granted file and passes only its name and at most 64 KiB of bytes. The callback receives no filesystem path. Its properties and issues are bounded and schema-checked; this API does not restore the removed built-in NBT viewer.
operations.Minecraft.Content.InspectWithProvider: Use a published format provider to inspect a caller-owned user-file grant. Directories and files over 64 KiB are rejected. The Host compares file revisions before and after the callback, permits at most 256 distinct named properties and 128 issues, and returns the typed result. Package-file access uses the separate verified-package API.
operations.Minecraft.Worlds.PlanDelete: Prepare removal of one admitted world at its current revision. Delete consumes this plan and moves the world into the instance content trash. It does not immediately erase the world bytes.
operations.Minecraft.Worlds.Delete: Consume a PlanDelete result after Host confirmation. The world/content owner verifies the world identity, revision, source file facts and running-game state. RestoreTrash can recover the moved directory; ClearTrash is a separate permanent operation.
operations.Minecraft.Worlds.ListBackups: List snapshots belonging to the admitted world. Returned backup IDs are caller-owned and specific to the world; they cannot be exchanged with general Backups IDs. A maximum of 256 snapshots is returned.
operations.Minecraft.Worlds.PrepareRestoreDestinati: Admit a new world name under the original instance’s saves directory, bound to the current world revision. The name must be a safe single path component and cannot begin with .nexa-. The destination must not exist. The returned EntityId is authority for PreviewRestore, not a path.
operations.Minecraft.Worlds.PreviewRestore: Prepare restoration using a backup returned by Worlds.ListBackups and a destination returned by Worlds.PrepareRestoreDestination for that same world. ExpectedRevision belongs to the backup; the destination separately binds the original world revision. The owner restores into a new directory and preserves the original world.
operations.Minecraft.Worlds.Restore: Consume the world restore plan after confirmation. The owner verifies the snapshot, refuses existing or linked destinations, restores to staging, validates level.dat and publishes the new directory. Running games and stale world revisions block restoration.
operations.Catalog.RegisterCollection: Publish an owned collection of at most 256 distinct resource references and 64 distinct tags. The collection becomes visible atomically with its plugin. ListCollections and ReadCollection consume the registration; stopping its owner removes it.
operations.Catalog.ListCollections: List active registered resource collections with revision-bound pagination. Staged registrations are not exposed. Collection membership is a resource reference, not proof that the resource is installed or downloadable.
operations.Catalog.ReadCollection: Read an active collection by qualified ID. A stopped or absent provider returns NOT_FOUND; callers must not reuse a cached collection as current authority.
operations.Catalog.RegisterTranslationProvider: Register kind nexa:catalog/translation with Translate: CatalogTranslationInput → CatalogTranslation. The input contains a validated project and requested locale; the output may change display name and summary only. It cannot change provider/project identity or download provenance.
operations.Catalog.ReadTranslatedProject: Resolve the original project through its catalog provider, then invoke the selected translation provider. Locales are 2–64 ASCII letters/digits/hyphens. Names are 1–1,024 characters and summaries at most 65,536 characters. Failure remains a failure; the caller may explicitly choose to show the untranslated project.
operations.Accounts.SignOut: Ask the Host to clear persisted access, refresh and provider credentials from the selected account record while retaining public profile metadata. The account owner checks roster CAS, advances credential generations, retires verified launch identities and clears selection if needed. Re-read Accounts.List afterward because account handles include the roster revision. This is local sign-out, not remote token revocation.
operations.Accounts.RegisterProvider: Register kind nexa:accounts/authentication with ResolveSignIn: SignInRequest → AccountProviderConfiguration. The supported protocols are yggdrasil and nide8 with an HTTPS auth server. BeginSignIn resolves this configuration and uses the existing Host onboarding flow. Credentials and tokens remain with that owner; callbacks cannot replace the resolved server during ContinueSignIn. Arbitrary OAuth implementations are outside this provider table.
operations.Settings.RegisterSchema: Stage a plugin-owned setting schema at version 1. Supported scopes are global and instance. ValueSchema and Default must validate against a known ABI schema. The Host stores values in a private durable namespace using canonical instance identity, revision CAS and explicit defaults. Use RegisterVersionedSchema before introducing a migration.
operations.Settings.RegisterVersionedSchema: Stage the current positive version of an owned SettingSchema. Registration does not transform persisted values. GetEffective rejects a stored value from another version until Migrate succeeds. The same plugin ID and setting ID retain their durable values across load replacement.
operations.Settings.RegisterPage: Register a verified NXML package page through the same rendering path as UI.RegisterPage. EntryFile must be an owned package-file handle. The page appears only after atomic activation and is removed on retirement. Registering a schema does not automatically generate controls.
operations.Settings.Migrate: Confirm a forward migration from the exact persisted FromVersion to the registered ToVersion. Handler receives SettingMigrationInput and returns a value matching the current setting schema. The callback is query-only and cannot mutate Host state. The Host rechecks schema identity and storage revision before one atomic write; failure or rejection preserves the old value. Repeating a completed migration returns a stale-version error.
operations.Themes.MigrateOptions: Validate and persist the supplied typed option values against the current theme manifest’s options schema and version. The operation uses the same owner revision and renderer-effect path as SaveOptions; it does not translate legacy configuration key names. Unknown or incompatible options are rejected and missing options retain compatible existing values/defaults. A successful Tasks result contains current ThemeOptions.
operations.Themes.ListResources: Copy resources explicitly declared as asset(...) in the current theme appearance. User-granted external files are not delegated to plugins. The owner verifies the source revision, containment and resource format, with limits of 128 resources, 16 MiB per item and 32 MiB total. Returned ThemeResource values and blobs belong to the calling load.
operations.Themes.ReadResource: Resolve an exact ThemeResource returned by ListResources to its owned BlobRef. A forged resource, another caller’s blob or a released resource is rejected. The returned bytes are an immutable copy, independent of a later theme reload.
operations.Themes.ReleaseResource: Release an owned theme blob and zero its retained bytes. Release is explicit and single-use; reads after release fail. Plugin retirement also releases retained application blobs.
operations.Backups.PrepareRestoreDestination: Admit an owned writable FileRef whose destination does not exist. Return a load-local destination EntityId for PreviewRestore. A raw path or an existing instance ID cannot replace this handle.
operations.Backups.ImportInto: Import a thin backup manifest from an owned readable FileRef into an explicitly admitted instance scope. This additive request works when that scope has no existing backup. The Host confirms import and uses the owner’s validated immutable manifest importer; duplicates and malformed records fail.
operations.Downloads.RegisterSourceResolver: Register kind nexa:downloads/source-resolver with Resolve: DownloadSource → DownloadSource. Resolve/Start invoke it for sources carrying this provider ID. The resolved source must be HTTP(S), contain no embedded credentials or fragment, and either use the Host transport or name a registered transfer provider. Resolver chaining is not recursive.
operations.Downloads.RegisterTransferProvider: Register kind nexa:downloads/transfer with ReadChunk: DownloadChunkRequest → DownloadChunk. Provider downloads require one resolved source, exact length and SHA-256. The Host requests sequential chunks of at most 64 KiB, validates offset/length/end, writes staging and verifies the full digest before publishing. Pause/cancel retire the attempt; resume restarts from zero. The provider never receives the destination path.
operations.Minecraft.Diagnostics.RegisterRuleProvid: Register kind nexa:diagnostics/rules with Analyze: InstanceSummary → DiagnosticAnalysis. AnalyzeWithProvider is the explicit consumer. The callback receives public instance metadata only; it does not acquire log, file or repair authority.
operations.Minecraft.Diagnostics.AnalyzeWithProvide: Invoke an active rule provider for an admitted instance and recheck its revision afterward. The result must name that instance and contain at most 128 reports and 128 issues. The Host namespaces report codes and overwrites correlation/operation IDs so a provider cannot impersonate Host diagnostics.
